name: Isack Lugata
hero: Hey! I'm Isack Lugata. I build websites, mobile apps, and AI-powered products that work for real people.
intro: Full-stack & mobile developer in Dar es Salaam. Co-founder of Ecofy Africa. Open to freelance projects.
aboutHero: I turn ambitious ideas into thoughtful digital products, from the interface to the systems behind it.
about: My route into software started with a simple habit: taking an idea apart until I understood how it worked. Computer Science at the University of Dar es Salaam gave that curiosity a foundation. Building real products taught me the rest: how to connect an interface to an API, untangle a backend, and turn a promising idea into something people can actually use.

Today I'm based in Dar es Salaam, working with founders and teams across agriculture, commerce, property, and legal technology. I co-founded Ecofy Africa and work across its frontend, backend, and AI. Elsewhere, my work has helped shape products including GloboExpats, Habitek, and Wakili Msomi, alongside backend systems for Osher Market, Falco, and TanStack Tanzania.

I work across frontend, mobile, backend, and applied AI, moving comfortably between the interface and the systems behind it. That range has taken me from community marketplaces and property platforms to legal assistants and internal management tools. My role changes with the project; the standard stays the same: understand the problem, make thoughtful decisions, and build something that holds together.

As chairperson of the UDSM 3D Solutions & Robotics Lab, I learned to bring people, ideas, and technical work into the same room. Our projects included Nena AI and TanStack Tanzania. I bring that same approach to client work today: collaborate closely, take ownership of my contribution, and care about the details that make a product feel finished.

services.description: Responsive websites, product interfaces, and web applications. Clear user journeys, thoughtful interaction, and frontend work connected to real APIs.

services.title: Mobile apps
services.description: Mobile applications built around clear interfaces, reliable APIs, and practical everyday workflows, from the first screen to the services behind it.

projects.name: Ecofy Africa
projects.summary: Ecofy Africa brings farm planning, activity records, and agricultural guidance into one product for Tanzanian farmers. I am a co-founder, CEO and AI Lead, and work on both the frontend and backend.
story: Ecofy starts with a practical challenge: helping a farmer understand what to do next. Planning a season, keeping records, and working with changing information all need to feel like one useful experience.

I work across the frontend and backend, alongside AI services and technical product direction. That means thinking about both the screen a farmer uses and the systems that turn information into guidance.

The product brings farm activity, seasonal tasks, weather, and market information together for Swahili-speaking users. Making those pieces work together requires attention to the farming context as well as the software.

Co-founding Ecofy has made product judgment part of my engineering work. I care about which problem a feature solves, how it fits into the rest of the platform, and what it asks of the person using it.
Ecofy is where my work as a developer and founder comes together: building a product, working with a team, and connecting technical decisions to an everyday need.
projects.role: Frontend & backend · Co-founder, CEO & AI Lead
projects.status: Public website and linked farm application

projects.name: Wakili Msomi
projects.summary: Wakili Msomi is an AI-powered legal-information application for the Tanzanian context. I worked on both its frontend and backend, connecting the user-facing experience with the services behind it.
story: Legal information is often difficult to navigate. Wakili Msomi brings AI-assisted legal information and document workflows into an application built for the Tanzanian context.
My contribution covered both the frontend and backend. I worked across the user-facing experience and the application services that support it, keeping the connection between the two in focus.
The project grew out of my practical-training experience at Bluefin Solutions, in collaboration with Sheria Kiganjani. English and Swahili users are part of the context behind the product.
The work brought together interfaces, APIs, document processing, and AI integration. It is the kind of project I enjoy: several technical layers serving one clear user experience.

projects.name: GloboExpats
projects.summary: GloboExpats is a marketplace for the expat community in Tanzania. My work is mainly on the frontend: the interfaces people use to browse, discover, buy, and sell.
story: GloboExpats is a marketplace built around the expat community in Tanzania, bringing goods, services, homes, vehicles, and community requests into one browsing experience.
My contribution is mainly frontend development. I work on the part of the product people navigate: turning platform features and data into interfaces that make sense together.
A marketplace has a lot to communicate at once. Categories, listings, seller information, and the next action all need enough space to be useful without competing for attention.
I approach that work through clarity and continuity: help someone understand what they are looking at, keep interactions predictable, and make the move from browsing to acting feel natural.
GloboExpats reflects the frontend side of my work: product interfaces connected to real services, with attention to both the broad journey and the small details along the way.

projects.name: Habitek
projects.summary: Habitek combines property discovery with property and hospitality management in Tanzania. I worked on both the frontend and backend of the platform.
story: Habitek connects property discovery with property and hospitality management in Tanzania. The product has to serve both someone looking for a place and the people responsible for managing it.

I worked on the frontend and backend, connecting the interfaces with the application services behind them. That shared view helps me think through a workflow from the first interaction to the underlying business logic.
From discovery to everyday management, the focus is a coherent product experience. Habitek is an example of how I work across the stack while keeping the user journey in view.

projects.name: Osher Market
projects.summary: Osher Market is a commerce and business platform. My contribution is backend development: the application services behind the marketplace experience.
story: Osher Market brings buyers, sellers, and business operations together in a commerce platform. Behind the storefront, the product depends on application services that keep those workflows connected.
My contribution is backend development. I work on the services and application logic that support the marketplace experience.
That work calls for clear boundaries between requests, business rules, and data. I focus on making the system understandable as a whole, rather than treating each endpoint as an isolated task.
Osher represents the operational side of my engineering work: building the foundations that allow a product interface to do something useful.

projects.name: Falco Finance
projects.summary: Falco Finance needed an internal management backend to support its day-to-day operations. I worked on the backend services and business logic behind that system.
story: My work with Falco focuses on its internal management system: the software supporting how the business organizes its everyday work.
I contributed backend development, working on the application services and business logic behind the management workflows.
Internal tools deserve the same care as public products. Clear rules, predictable behavior, and maintainable services make a difference to the people who rely on them.
The project reflects a part of my work that sits behind the scenes: turning business needs into a backend that a team can work with and build on.

projects.name: TanStack Tanzania
projects.summary: TanStack Tanzania connects tech students with opportunities, learning resources, and career support. I worked on its backend as part of our lab's project work.
story: TanStack Tanzania connects tech students with opportunities, learning resources, companies, and career support. It brings several useful starting points for a technical career into one platform.
My contribution is backend development for the platform. I work on the services behind its student-facing experience.
TanStack is also part of our work at the UDSM 3D Solutions & Robotics Lab, alongside projects such as Nena AI. It connects software development with a community I know first-hand.
For me, the project brings two interests together: building useful systems and making technical opportunities easier for people to find.
